request.text:
Refine the current Builder Prototype UI 050 for the accepted change-oriented workflow.

1. Replace the static mock `builder-chat` history and local-only submit action with the canonical durable AdaOS conversation binding already supported by the installed client/runtime. The selected project topic/thread are authoritative: use page state `builderTopicId` and `builderThreadId`, and the Builder conversation id. Submitting in the Prototype lane must invoke `builder_skill.chat` exactly once and persist one canonical user message plus one canonical assistant response. This is a narrowly scoped internal development control-plane exception; do not add external network, credential, device, or project production-data bindings.
2. Display exactly one Conversation section according to the selected dependent Lifecycle node. Prototype: interactive Builder chat plus Development settings. Automation: its durable task/thread, follow-up form, status/evidence, and no Development settings. Publication: read-only publication evidence and no mutation controls. Keep one compact tab label `Conversation`, not three competing toolbar sections.
3. Preserve the dependent Prototype -> Automation -> Publication information model, exact preview selection, initial Yjs state mapping, current layout, en/ru locales, and valid UTF-8. Do not manually edit version or updated_at; Forge owns them.
4. Treat a return-to-prototype adaptation task as transition evidence, not as a second Automation release. The visible lifecycle must not show two Automation rows with the same semantic version for one source Prototype. A brand-new template project must still show one Prototype revision and no Automation until a real handoff/task exists.
5. Add declarative scenario tests for the durable chat binding, lane-dependent single Conversation surface, and absence of duplicate semantic Automation rows. Do not publish, activate, commit, or push repositories. Report any generic client/control ABI gap instead of inventing a scenario-local workaround.
